extraction.name: MINT-1T
extraction.description: MINT-1T is the most extensive and diverse open-source Multimodal INTerleaved dataset comprising one trillion text tokens and 3.4 billion images. The dataset includes previously untapped sources such as PDFs and ArXiv papers, sourced from HTML documents, PDFs, and ArXiv papers from CommonCrawl and ArXiv dumps.
extraction.creator: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, Ludwig Schmidt
extraction.publisher: University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, University of California Berkeley
extraction.citeAs: Anas Awadalla et al. MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv:2406.11271v5 [cs.CV] 31 Oct 2024
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected from CommonCrawl WARC files (HTML documents from May 2017 to April 2024), CommonCrawl WAT files (PDF documents from February 2023 to April 2024), and ArXiv LaTeX source code. HTML documents were parsed using DOM tree extraction. PDFs were downloaded and read using PyMuPDF, extracting reading order based on text block bounding boxes and clustering. ArXiv documents were built from LaTeX source code using TexSoup to find figure tags and interleave images with paper text.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: HTML documents sourced from CommonCrawl WARC files (May 2017 to April 2024 dumps, with full dumps from October 2018 to April 2024 and partial dumps from earlier years). PDF documents sourced from CommonCrawl WAT files (February 2023 to April 2024 dumps). ArXiv documents sourced from ArXiv S3 buckets containing LaTeX source code.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Data collection occurred from January 2024 to June 2024. The dataset includes web data from 2013 to 2024, with HTML documents from May 2017 to April 2024 and PDF documents from February 2023 to April 2024.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Non-English documents were removed using Fasttext's language identification model (confidence threshold 0.65). Documents with URLs containing NSFW substrings were removed. Text filtering methods from RefinedWeb were applied, removing documents with excessive duplicate n-grams or identified as low quality using MassiveText rules. Images smaller than 150 pixels or larger than 20,000 pixels were removed. For HTML, images with aspect ratio greater than 2 were removed; for PDFs, this threshold was adjusted to 3. PDFs larger than 50MB or over 50 pages were discarded. Pages with no text were excluded. Email addresses were replaced with templates like 'email@example.com' and IP addresses with randomly generated non-functional IPs.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Fasttext for language identification, NSFW image detector for safety filtering, PyMuPDF for PDF parsing, TexSoup for ArXiv LaTeX parsing
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be updated by the authors. Updates will be communicated through the README in the Huggingface interface. Older versions can be found using Git history of the dataset repository. Issues with previous versions will be communicated in the erratum. A Google form will be provided to remove samples from MINT-1T upon request.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset may contain personally identifiable information, images of individuals, and text about specific individuals as it is sourced from the public web. Email addresses and IP addresses were masked to remove personal data. The dataset may contain sensitive information including race or ethnic origins, sexual orientations, religious beliefs, political opinions, locations, financial or health data, and criminal history if present on the public web.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset was built to make research into large multimodal models more accessible. Using the dataset to train models that ingest or generate personally identifying information (such as images of people's faces and other sensitive content) as well as military applications are inappropriate use cases.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors follow previous works in not using text quality classifier models as they have been shown to favor text from certain demographics. While steps were taken to reduce biases and risks, dataset consumers are encouraged to further filter the data based on their use case.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: PDF parsing has limitations: sometimes unable to detect images and may extract incorrect reading order due to arbitrary PDF layouts. This compromise between speed and accuracy is a noted limitation. The dataset relies on downloading external image URLs which may not remain available over time due to link rot. The dataset may contain confidential content and offensive, insulting, or threatening content despite filtering efforts. Future work should explore more ways to improve the safety of multimodal internet data and develop fast, robust methods for determining reading order across diverse document layouts.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for pre-training large multimodal models that can process multiple interleaved images and text. Use cases include Training, Testing, and Validation of large multimodal models. The dataset can also be used for generating interleaved images and text sequences or for building multimodal document retrieval systems. Models trained on MINT-1T were evaluated on in-context learning tasks, captioning benchmarks (COCO, TextCaps), visual question answering datasets (VQAv2, OK-VQA, TextVQA, VizWiz), and multi-image reasoning benchmarks (MMMU, Mantis-Eval).
